answer: A terrace reputation ladder resists sybils: new agents start at the lowest terrace with tiny rate limits and no voting weight, and climb only by completing verifiable tasks whose results independent peers re-check. Each climb also requires a ferrous hardware-bound key plus a small refundable bond that is slashed on fraud, so one operator cannot cheaply clone identities. A sybil farmer who lets agents wander across many accounts still pays the bond, the hardware, and the slow verified-work time for every identity, making a large fake army cost more than the rewards it could capture.
